slots.brief: Given the half-life, find the mean life (or vice versa) of a radionuclide; single relation τ = T½/ln2.
Circuit with a diode in series with resistors; use the diode's forward voltage drop to find the current through the branch; requires circuit figure.
Person in an accelerating lift; ask for the normal reaction (apparent weight) for upward or downward acceleration.
Given horizontal and vertical components of Earth's field, find the angle of dip using tanθ = Bv/BH.
Body covers half the total distance at one speed and half at another; ask the average speed over the whole journey.

slots.subtopic: Mean free path / mean free time
slots.brief: Ask how mean free path changes when temperature is raised at constant pressure (or diameter/molecule count changed); requires careful λ ∝ T/(p·d²) reasoning.
Two wires of same material but different lengths and areas support the same load; find the ratio of elongations, or find which parameter changes under combined conditions.
Convert a temperature reading between two scales using the linear-interpolation formula; simple two-point mapping.
Wire stretched so its length increases by a given factor; find new resistance using R ∝ L² at constant volume.
Circular coil with given turns, current and area (or radius); compute the magnetic dipole moment NIA.
Give a standard y(x,t) sinusoidal equation; ask for amplitude, wavelength, frequency or wave speed by comparing with the standard form.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Given work function and incident photon wavelength, find the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons; direct Einstein equation plug-in.
Body starting from rest with uniform acceleration; find distance covered in a specific (nth) second using the nth-second formula.
System of point masses placed at corners of a simple square/line; find the coordinates of the centre of mass.
Electron in a hydrogen-like atom jumps between two given levels; find the emitted photon energy or wavelength using Bohr energy formula.
Body projected from a planet's surface; use energy conservation with the escape-energy expression to find maximum height or impact speed; multi-step reasoning.
Concave mirror forms an image with given magnification (sign tells real/virtual); solve mirror formula plus magnification relation for object distance and focal length.
Quantity computed as a product/quotient of measured values (e.g. density from mass and radius); find the maximum percentage error by adding relative errors.
Show a gate combination (e.g. NAND/NOR wiring) or name a gate; ask which output column matches the circuit — no figure needed if gate symbols described in options.
Series LCR with given R, L, C and source frequency; compute the impedance (and optionally power factor) by direct formula.
Capacitor network with some series and parallel elements; redraw the circuit and find the equivalent capacitance between two terminals; circuit figure required.
Source moving toward then away from a stationary observer at the same speed; ask the ratio of the two observed frequencies.
Soap bubble of given radius and surface tension; find the excess pressure inside using 4S/r; diagram can show the bubble with inner/outer radii.
Magnetic flux varies with time as a polynomial/sinusoid; differentiate the flux expression and evaluate the induced emf at a specified instant.

slots.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slots.brief: EM wave of given intensity falls on a perfectly absorbing (or reflecting) surface; find the radiation pressure or force on the surface.
Standard YDSE with given slit separation and screen distance; compute fringe width, or number of fringes in a given screen length.
Balanced Wheatstone bridge circuit with four resistances and a galvanometer; find the unknown resistance for balance (or current in the bridge arm when unbalanced); circuit figure required.
PV diagram of a closed cycle (rectangle or triangle) given; ask for net work done over the cycle by computing the enclosed area; figure shows the cycle.
Rotating body (e.g. dancer or disc with dropped mass) changes its moment of inertia; use angular momentum conservation to find the new angular speed.
Astronomical telescope with given objective and eyepiece focal lengths; find magnifying power and tube length (or find focal lengths given both quantities).
Given the temperature of a gas, find the average translational kinetic energy per molecule (or total for given moles) using (3/2)kT.
Path difference at a point on the screen given in terms of wavelength; decide whether the point is a maximum/minimum or find the intensity ratio using I = 4I₀cos²(φ/2).
Charged particle enters a magnetic field with given velocity direction and field direction; ask the direction of the magnetic force (zero/along which axis) using the cross-product rule.
Two bodies with equal kinetic energies (or equal momenta) but different masses; find the ratio of their momenta (or kinetic energies) using p = √(2mK).
Two or three fixed point charges exert forces on a test charge; find where the net force is zero, or compute the resultant force magnitude by vector addition.
Block or knot under three forces shown in a diagram (e.g. hanging weight with two ropes at angles); resolve components to find an unknown tension; diagram required.
Two stars orbiting their common centre of mass; relate orbital radii to masses and derive/find the orbital period or speed symbolically; multi-step gravitational reasoning.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Two particles (e.g. electron and proton) accelerated through the same potential difference; compare their de Broglie wavelengths using λ ∝ 1/√(mK).
Springs in series/parallel (or a spring cut into pieces) attached to a mass; find the equivalent spring constant and the new time period of oscillation.
Charged conductor or symmetric distribution (sphere/cylinder); use Gauss's law to reason where the field is zero or which surface encloses the charge — conceptual symmetry selection.
Give radius ratio scenario or an ionic compound in an hcp/fcc lattice; ask how many octahedral and tetrahedral voids per unit cell / per atom, or which voids are occupied to give the formula
Provide a Lewis/structure figure of two simple species (e.g., one hypervalent molecule); ask students to pick the correct geometry or hybridisation from drawn options
Ask which ligands are weak-field vs strong-field from the spectrochemical series, or the colour/magnetic nature a given series implies
Give a complex (3d metal with ligands of mixed field strength); ask for the d-orbital configuration, spin state and unpaired electron count
Match vitamins as fat/water soluble or list deficiency disease / chemical name of a given vitamin
Ask to identify the functional group or general rule from nomenclature for a simple branched compound (e.g., naming with lowest locants)
Give Kc for a gaseous equilibrium; ask for Kp using Δn and the relation Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn with a stated temperature
Ask the structure/hybridisation and shape of xenon fluoride(s) (e.g., XeF4 or XeOF4) with lone-pair counting; could combine with a statement-evaluation option set
Show a figure of a substrate with a bulky/unsymmetrical alkyl group; choose the correct halide + alkoxide combination for Williamson synthesis
Combustion analysis or reaction of a compound: given masses of products, find the mass of an element or moles of a reactant consumed
Brown ring test: ask which ion is confirmed and the formula of the coloured complex responsible
Ask which disaccharide/sugar on hydrolysis gives which monosaccharides, or identify a non-reducing sugar with reasoning from glycosidic linkage
Give an orbital designation (e.g., 3d or 4f); ask the possible/values of n, l, m and number of orbitals, or which quantum numbers are invalid
Cannizzaro reaction of a given aldehyde: identify which moiety becomes the alcohol and which the acid (no numbers)
Graham's law: compare rates of effusion of two gases to find molar mass ratio or time ratio
Given a figure of amines, identify which responds to the carbylamine test (or order basicity in aqueous vs gas phase) with structure-based reasoning
A statement about what happens to equilibrium position/K when pressure or inert gas is added or temperature changed; pick correct effect on K and yield
Show a figure of an ozonolysis: given ozonolysis products (carbonyls), reconstruct the alkene structure
Given Λm° values of ions by Kohlrausch's law, calculate limiting molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte (e.g., an acid) by linear combination
Given i for an electrolyte or compare i values across dissociation/association cases; ask which solution shows maximum boiling point elevation at same molality
First-order kinetics: given initial amount and amount after a time (or half-life), find the rate constant or fraction remaining
Cleavage of an unsymmetrical/mixed ether with excess HI; show structure figure and ask which alkyl iodide and alcohol form
Magnetic moment of a given transition-metal ion: write d configuration and count unpaired electrons / compute √n(n+2)
Rank a set of elements by ionisation enthalpy or electron gain enthalpy (e.g., noble gases vs halogens vs group 2) and pick correct order
Four statements on adsorption (physisorption vs chemisorption, Freundlich log-log line slope, effect of temperature) – mark true/false combination
Ionic vs covalent/metallic hydrides: identify properties like thermal stability trend down a group or electrical conductivity
Photochemical smog or ozone-depletion: which pollutants (NOx, CFCs, PAN) contribute and the reactions involved
Given mean bond enthalpies and ΔH of reaction (or ΔH and all but one bond enthalpy), find the missing bond enthalpy via Hess cycle
Bohr radius/energy for hydrogen-like ion: ratio question (radius in n=2 of He+ vs n=2 of H) using Z²/Z scaling
Give formulae of 2–3 complexes; ask which pair exhibits ionisation/hydrate/linkage isomerism
Match artificial sweeteners (aspartame, saccharin, sucralose) with their use or structure class
Order given species by bond angle or bond length (e.g., NO2+/NO2/NO2– or NH3/PH3 series) using hybridisation/lone-pair logic
Given standard electrode potentials of a few metals, rank their reducing strength or pick which reaction is feasible (compare E° pairs)
Multi-statement question on diborane structure/reactions (banana bonds, hydrolysis, reaction with water/ammonia); pick the correct combination of true statements

slots.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slots.brief: Rank alkenes by heat of hydrogenation / stability (cis-trans-substituted comparison); pick correct increasing or decreasing order
Order alkyl halides by SN1 or SN2 reactivity (e.g., methyl/1°/2°/3°/allylic) with justification via carbocation stability
Across the 3d series, which ion has maximum unpaired electrons / highest oxidation state in common compounds (e.g., Mn); simple trend + count
Figure-based Fischer projection: assign R/S configuration to each stereocentre and match with given options
Elimination followed by HBr addition (Markovnikov/anti-Markovnikov with peroxide): trace the final product through a two-step sequence
Allotropes of sulphur (rhombic vs monoclinic – stability ranges, transition temperature) as simple fact recall
5-sentence para jumble on a simple descriptive theme (e.g., a festival or a morning routine); ask for the correct order of the jumbled sentences; keep logical connectors obvious for easy level.
Ask the meaning of a common everyday idiom (e.g., 'to let the cat out of the bag') used in a short sentence; four options give meanings, one is correct.
Convert a simple present or past tense sentence from active to passive voice (or identify the correct passive form among options); use a transitive verb with a clear object.
Sentence divided into four parts; error in subject-verb agreement (e.g., 'each of the boys were'); 'No error' included as an option to keep difficulty moderate.
Single-blank sentence completion testing a moderately difficult vocabulary word (e.g., 'candid', 'deter'); context clue in the sentence should point to the correct meaning.
Spot the error in a sentence testing tense consistency across clauses (e.g., past event mixed with present tense); include 'No error' as an option.
Easy fill-in-the-blank testing the correct preposition with a common verb/phrase (e.g., 'insist on', 'afraid of'); four simple preposition options.
Verbal analogy pair (e.g., 'Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?'); choose the option that preserves the same relationship; use a familiar, high-yield analogy type.
PQRS para jumble where first and last sentences (P and S positions) are given; test taker orders the two middle sentences; short narrative paragraph for easy level.
Pick the antonym of a common word given in isolation or in a short sentence (e.g., antonym of 'abundant'); distractors are near-synonyms or unrelated words.
Improve the underlined gerund-after-preposition construction (e.g., 'interested to learn' → 'interested in learning'); choose the grammatically correct improved version.
Pick the synonym of a common everyday word (e.g., synonym of 'generous' or 'brave'); four simple options, one clearly correct.
Easy two-blank or single-blank sentence completion with everyday vocabulary; the sentence context should make the correct word obvious among the four options.
Two- or three-line statement about a family (e.g., pointing to a photograph); ask how many males / how many cousins are there in the given relation chain.
A word is coded by shifting each letter by a fixed pattern or using positional values with an arithmetic twist (e.g., reverse alphabet); ask the code for a new word.
Two straightforward universal statements with clear overlap; ask which conclusions definitely follow (no 'possibility' cases).
Four words where three share a category (e.g., types of a fruit/occupation) and one differs; pick the odd one.
Ask which of five given words would appear first (or last) in dictionary order, possibly with close spellings to increase difficulty.
Alpha-numeric series combining letters with a numeric pattern (e.g., AB2, CD4, EF6...); find the next term.
Letter analogy based on position in the alphabet (e.g., B : D :: C : ?) or a small number analogy like 9 : 81.
Find the condition on k so that the line y = kx + c is tangent to a given circle; ask for the tangency relation or the number of tangent lines from an external point
Direct limit of (1 - cos x)/x^2 type or sin(ax)/sin(bx) as x tends to 0; student must pick the correct standard form
Solve a homogeneous differential equation dy/dx = f(x,y) with degree-1 RHS using the substitution y = vx and integrate
Find the intervals in which a given polynomial or rational function is increasing/decreasing by examining f'(x)
Given three vectors, compute the scalar triple product [a b c] and identify a property (volume, coplanarity) from it
Two-draw or card-die scenario; ask P(A|B) or check independence of two events from a joint table
Definite integral of an odd or even trig function over symmetric limits; student uses symmetry then a standard result
Classic rate of change: water draining from a conical tank or balloon inflating; relate dV/dt to dr/dt via chain rule
Area bounded by a parabola and a straight line (or y = f(x) with y = g(x)); set up and evaluate the difference integral
Arrange letters of a word so that certain vowels are always together and a particular pair never together; combine cases carefully
Line through the intersection of two given lines and a fixed point; use the family-of-lines form and solve for the parameter
Given a general second-degree equation in x, y, complete the square to find the centre and radius of the circle it represents
Given lines in symmetric form, check whether they intersect / are coplanar via the determinant condition and find the answer option
Quadratic with roots of opposite sign / both roots greater than a number; use location-of-roots conditions on discriminant and f at endpoints
Evaluate a 3x3 determinant using row/column operations (splitting a row as a sum) and factor the result

slots.subtopic: Perpendicular distance from point to line
slots.brief: Find the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a line given in 3D vector form; ask for the coordinates
Selection problem: choose a committee of fixed size with at least/axactly some constraint; count with combination sums
Simplify |z1 z2| / |z1| type expression or find a z satisfying a modulus equation using modulus-conjugate relations
Find the domain of a rational + square-root composite function; intersect conditions from numerator and denominator
Set operations: given cardinalities of A, B and their intersection/union, find cardinality of a combination using Venn-type identities
Multi-step vector identity problem: use cross product, then compute a vector triple product or find a vector satisfying given dot/cross conditions

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Find the image of a point in a given line using the reflection formula; verify by checking the midpoint lies on the line
Form the differential equation of a family y = Ae^{kx} + B (or similar) by eliminating arbitrary constants
Use sum-to-product or conditional identity to evaluate a trig expression given a relation between angles (e.g., tan A + tan B given)
Solve a basic trig equation like sin x = -1/2 or 2cos^2 x = 1 and state the general solution in terms of n and π
Given a function f(x) (e.g., f(x) = x + 1/x style), check whether it is one-one/onto and find its inverse if it exists
Evaluate a composite like sin^{-1}(sin x) outside the principal range or tan^{-1}a + tan^{-1}b using the right-triangle method and quadrant care
Simplify a product of complex numbers given in polar/rectangular form; find the modulus and argument of the result
Find the equation of a parabola with given focus and directrix (or vertex and axis), then answer a property of it
Find the term independent of x (or coefficient of x^k) in the expansion of (x^a + b/x^c)^n using the general term
Coins/dice classical probability: count favourable outcomes over total, e.g. at least one head or a sum condition on two dice
Binomial distribution: given n, p and a target number of successes, compute P(X = k) or the mean/variance
Find local maxima/minima of a cubic or a trig-rational function: differentiate, solve f'(x)=0, classify with sign of f''
For a square matrix A, use adj/transpose properties (e.g., det(adj A), (AB)^T = B^T A^T) to evaluate an expression; include a trick like A being singular
Simple indefinite integral of the form ∫ f(ax+b) dx or ∫ x^k e^{x^{k+1}} type solved by direct substitution
Given a small frequency/ungrouped data set, compute mean deviation about the mean (or median) step by step
For an implicit curve like x^3 + y^3 = 3axy, find dy/dx at a given point or where the tangent is horizontal
Piecewise function with parameters k and m: enforce continuity and differentiability at the joint to solve for the constants
Verify whether a given relation on a small set is reflexive/symmetric/transitive, or count functions from one set to another
Sum an arithmetico-geometric series of the form a + (a+d)r + (a+2d)r^2 + ... using the standard shift-and-subtract method
Use (1+x)^n expansion with x = ±1 or i to find a sum of alternate binomial coefficients or C0+C2+C4+...
Simple distance-formula application: distance between two points in 3D, or distance of a point from an axis, by direct substitution
Two 2x2 (or 3x3) matrices given; compute a product like AB or (AB)^2 and read off an entry or trace
Definite/indefinite integral needing integration by parts (log x or inverse trig times x) or a partial-fraction split
Area between two curves where symmetry about an axis halves the work (e.g., y^2 = 4ax cut by a line); evaluate via splitting at the axis
